assessments.reasoning: Chapter 5 describes the local transformation of the matched fragment when its rule condition is satisfied. Section 5.3 separately makes the frozen position prohibition applicable across rewrite strategies, and Section 4.4.9 treats the frozen argument root as part of the prohibited proper subtree. The precise premise incorporates this scope and keeps the transition possible rather than guaranteed.

challenge.method: Compare the Chapter 5 matching and condition paragraph to Sections 4.4.9 and 5.3. Consider an otherwise matching rule at a frozen argument root, within that argument, and at its enclosing operator root. Cross-check admissibility and execution strategy.
challenge.results: The first two positions lie inside the frozen argument subterm, so the exact condition excludes both. The enclosing operator root is distinct and can remain eligible when the applicable rule permits it. The otherwise-permitted premise keeps executable-rule restrictions; possible describes the transition relation without asserting a particular strategy or that the engine takes the step.

limitations: Documentary evidence from the exact Maude 3.5.1 manual supports a possible local transition. The verdict makes no implementation test, cross-edition, strategy, fairness or occurrence claim.
